activities.title: Story, what happens next
activities.intro: Listen to the story. Tap the card that shows what happens next.
activities.offScreen: Go tell a grown-up a short story about an animal, and what happens next.

rounds.prompt: The bird is hungry. The bird looks down. The bird sees a worm. What happens next?
The flower is thirsty. The sky turns grey. Rain begins to fall. What happens next?
The sun is high in the sky. It slowly goes down. The sky turns dark. What happens next?
The bird sits on her nest. She keeps the egg warm. The egg begins to crack. What happens next?

activities.title: Put the story in order
activities.intro: Listen to the story. Put the cards in order: first, then, next.
activities.offScreen: Go find a grown-up and tell them a short story with a beginning, a middle and an end.

rounds.prompt: First the bird is hungry. Then the bird finds a worm. Next the bird eats the worm. Put the cards in order: first, then, next.
First the sky turns grey. Then the rain falls. Next the flower drinks the rain. Put the cards in order: first, then, next.
First the sun is high. Then the sun goes down. Next the stars come out. Put the cards in order: first, then, next.

activities.title: What does it need
activities.intro: Listen for who needs something. Tap the thing they need.
activities.offScreen: Go find a plant or a pet in your home, and tell a grown-up what it needs.

rounds.prompt: A fish needs water to swim in. Tap the thing the fish needs.
A bird needs a nest to sleep in. Tap the thing the bird needs.
A flower needs sun to grow. Tap the thing the flower needs.
A seed needs rain to grow into a flower. Tap the thing the seed needs.

parentCard.title: Story questions
steps: Pick a picture book with a clear story, one they have not heard before if you can.
Read a page or two, then stop and ask why do you think that happened.
Read on a bit further, then stop again and ask why do you think the character did that.
Near the end, stop once more and ask why do you think the story ends this way.
Finish the book together and talk about what happened first, then and next.
notice: Do they answer with a guess about how the character feels, or just describe what they see on the page?
Do they ask their own question about the story?
